source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Numbers 19–24 aligns directly with Hebrew Numbers 19–24. All 182 original records, including every annotation, are hashed exactly. Later numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves the narrator’s explicit identification of previous omen-seeking and the new orientation.
Preserves the repeated declaration formula and marks the disputed opened/closed eye expression in a note.
Keeps Shaddai as Almighty and falling without asserting a trance; preserves uncovered eyes linking the earlier narrative.
Keeps all four plant and landscape comparisons, including difficult aloes, rather than substituting a familiar modern garden plant.
Retains seed’s agricultural and descendant associations, the pinned name Agag and the rising-kingdom parallel.
Retains singular pronouns, wild ox and violent victory images; arrows clause is difficult and its rendering is noted rather than silently emended.
Keeps the future action directed against Balak’s people; days to come does not impose a specific end-times system.
Preserves the repeated identification and eye formula with the same lexical decision as verse 3.
Keeps the added knowledge line, both divine titles and the repeated falling/eyes language without an unmarked trance claim.
Retains distant vision, star and scepter; chooses head-temples for corners, preserves pinned qarqar as devastate and uncertain Sheth as a name rather than silently emending the line.
Keeps the repeated possession claim and treats the plural enemies as a collective description of Seir, without changing the territorial object.
Preserves first without specifying chronological origin or political ranking, and keeps the first/end contrast.
Preserves Kain and Asshur names, retaining the difficult time-question rather than forcing a certain identification of Asshur or a duration.
Keeps the lament and question about survival without assigning an unexpressed modern event.
Preserves Kittim, both oppressed names and the final singular pronoun’s uncertain referent rather than resolving the historical sequence dogmatically.
